name: bet365
desc: Online sports betting, casino, poker and bingo operator run by the Coates family from Stoke-on-Trent.
capacity_detail: Revenue GBP 4bn and pre-tax profit GBP 349m in fiscal 2024
sponsorships: UFC official sports betting partner in US and Canada (multiyear, from Mar 2026); Stoke City shirt sponsor (from 2012) and Bet365 Stadium naming
markets: UK, US states, Canada (Ontario), Brazil, France, Colombia, Australia, Malta, Gibraltar, Bulgaria; exited China in 2025

signals.regions: Launched in France with sports, horse-race and poker licences (May 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bet365)

rationale: Global brand already paying for UFC in North America; F1 offers worldwide reach as UK Premier League front-of-shirt gambling sponsorship is banned from 2026-27.

name: Betfred
desc: UK bookmaker with over 1,650 shops, online betting and the Tote on-course pool betting business.
capacity_detail: Turnover GBP 8.8bn in the year to September 2022 (as reported)
sponsorships: Super League rugby league title partner; World Snooker Championship; Betfred British Masters golf (2024); PDC World Matchplay to 2025; US: Denver Broncos, Cincinnati Bengals, Colorado Rockies
markets: UK retail shops and racecourses, online via Gibraltar entity, and US sports betting via Betfredsports.com
rationale: Founder-owned bookmaker with big sports-title habit (snooker, golf, rugby league); F1 hospitality and UK/US audiences fit its sponsorship style.

name: BoyleSports
desc: Irish bookmaker with over 380 betting shops plus online sports betting, casino, poker and bingo.
capacity_detail: Principal partner and front-of-shirt sponsor of West Ham United for the 2025-26 Premier League season (announced July 2025)
sponsorships: West Ham United principal partner (2025); Newcastle United UK and Ireland betting partner (from 2021); Irish Grand National (from 2014); Irish Greyhound Derby; Grand Slam of Darts 2020
markets: Ireland, Northern Ireland and Great Britain through retail branches and online betting
rationale: Big spender on football and racing; with Premier League front-of-shirt betting deals banned from 2026-27, F1 is an alternative UK and Ireland showcase.

name: Parimatch
desc: Sports betting brand founded in Kyiv, now Cyprus-based and licensed in several countries and under Curacao.
capacity_detail: Leeds United sleeve partner and Manchester United partner across Asia and MENA (2025); UFC official Asia partner (2025)
sponsorships: Leeds United sleeve (2025); Manchester United Asia and MENA partner (2025); UFC Asia partner (2025); Joburg Super Kings principal partner (2025); Argentine FA (2024)
markets: Cyprus, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Tanzania and other African markets, Asia via partners, Curacao-licensed international site
rationale: Sole owner Sergey Portnov already buys global football and UFC rights in Asia; F1's Asian and Middle East races match its target markets.

name: Kaizen Gaming (Betano)
desc: Owner of the Betano online sports betting and gaming brand, active in about 20 markets in Europe and the Americas.
capacity_detail: Betano quarterly revenue EUR 788m in Q1 2026, up 27%
sponsorships: FIFA World Cup 2026 tournament supporter; UEFA EURO 2028 official sponsor; FC Bayern Munich; Aston Villa sleeve (2026-27); Tottenham Hotspur; Sporting CP and FC Porto shirt (2025-26); Benfica sleeve; River Plate; Sparta Prague
markets: Greece, Cyprus, Portugal, Romania, Bulgaria, Czechia, Germany, UK, Denmark, Belgium, Canada, Nigeria, Brazil, Argentina, Peru, Colombia, Chile, Ecuador
rationale: Betano already buys FIFA, UEFA and top-club deals; F1 adds global motorsport reach now Premier League limits betting brands to sleeves.

name: Stake (Easygo)
desc: Online casino and sportsbook Stake.com, built and serviced by Melbourne-based Easygo, which also runs the Kick streaming site.
capacity_detail: Everton sleeve sponsor for 2026-27 after front-of-shirt deal from 2022-23; UFC official betting partner
sponsorships: Everton front of shirt (2022-26) then sleeve (2026-27); UFC official betting partner (2022); Alfa Romeo/Sauber F1 title partner 2023-2025 (ended)
markets: Curacao-licensed global site plus licences in Colombia, Italy, Peru, Brazil, Denmark, Mexico, Greenland; US via Stake.us sweepstakes
rationale: Former Sauber title partner (to 2025) knows F1's value; Easygo revenue about A$970m. UK site shut in 2025 after regulator action, limiting UK exposure.

name: Gauselmann Group (Merkur)
industry: gaming machines, arcades and online gaming
desc: Family-owned German maker of Merkur slot machines that also runs arcades, casinos and online gaming sites.
sponsorships: Merkur Spiel-Arena naming rights (Fortuna Duesseldorf); RB Leipzig; Arminia Bielefeld; FC Schalke 04; Merkur Ostseehalle Kiel naming (10 years from Apr 2026)
markets: Germany core market, Europe under Merkur brand, UK via Praesepe, US via Gaming Arts; French casino acquisition pending
rationale: Family group with multi-billion revenue and German football sponsorship habit; F1 could carry the Merkur brand into its new UK, US and French businesses.

name: Novomatic
desc: Austrian gaming machine maker and operator of Admiral casinos, arcades and the Greentube online gaming business.
markets: About 2,000 venues in some 45-50 countries; mainly Austria, Germany, Italy, UK, Eastern Europe, plus France casinos and Ainsworth in Australia
rationale: Founder Johann Graf's group sells machines across 50 countries; F1 hospitality suits B2B selling to casino operators worldwide.

name: PMU (Pari Mutuel Urbain)
desc: French horse-race pool betting operator owned by racing societies, also offering online sports betting and poker.
capacity_detail: Stakes of about EUR 10bn and net result EUR 827m in 2022
markets: 13,200 points of sale in France and overseas territories; partner operations in UK, Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, Japan and Africa
rationale: Largest French betting network seeking growth in online sports betting; F1's French audience fits, but French regulator ANJ reviews operators' promotional strategies.

name: Codere
desc: Spanish gaming group running slot halls, betting and casinos in Spain, Italy and Latin America.
ownership: private, owner not stated (bondholders took 95% in restructuring)
sponsorships: Real Madrid official betting house (2016, three seasons)
markets: Spain, Italy, Mexico, Panama, Colombia, Argentina and Uruguay; online through its Codere Online subsidiary
rationale: Delisted since 2022 and bondholder-owned; Mexico City GP and Latin American race audience match its core markets.

name: VGW
desc: Operator of Chumba Casino, LuckyLand Slots and Global Poker sweepstakes games, mainly for US players.
capacity_detail: Revenue about A$7.3bn (US$4.76bn) in year to 30 June 2025
markets: United States sweepstakes casino and poker players, run from Australia; brands include Chumba, LuckyLand and Global Poker

signals.marketing: Former CMO Mats Johnson took over day-to-day leadership after founder stepped back (Jan 2026; https://sweepskings.com/news/vgw-chumba-post-record-revenue-2025/)

rationale: US$4.76bn revenue from US players; F1's US races could build brand, but more than ten US states have restricted sweepstakes gaming.

name: Dream Sports (Dream11)
desc: Indian fantasy sports platform Dream11, operated by Sporta Technologies under parent Dream Sports.
capacity_detail: Raised USD 840m in 2021 round led by Tiger Global, D1, Falcon Edge, DST and Redbird
sponsorships: India national cricket team lead jersey sponsor (Jul 2023-Mar 2026); IPL title sponsor 2020; New Zealand Super Smash title sponsor through 2026; NBA (2017)
markets: India-focused fantasy cricket and other sports; paid contests paused after August 2025 real-money gaming ban
rationale: Heavy sports sponsor in India; India's 2025 ban on real-money online games removed over 90% of revenue, so F1 spend is unlikely near term.

name: Lottoland
desc: Gibraltar-based online operator taking bets on the outcomes of lotteries worldwide, plus casino games.
markets: Australia, UK, Ireland, Italy, South Africa, India, Germany (GGL licence 2024) and Sweden
rationale: International lottery betting brand already naming Australian sports venue; F1 races in Australia and Europe match its markets.

name: Kalshi
desc: US federally regulated exchange where users trade event contracts, mostly on sports outcomes.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 22bn after TCV-led round, May 2026
sponsorships: NHL official prediction market partner (multiyear, Oct 2025); CNN and CNBC (2025); Fox News (2026)
markets: United States nationwide, with sports making up most activity; state actions in Nevada, Massachusetts, Ohio, Washington and others

signals.raise: TCV-led round at USD 22bn valuation (May 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalshi)

rationale: Sports drive 89% of revenue and it already pays the NHL; F1's growing US fan base fits, though several states are suing over sports contracts.

name: Polymarket
desc: Prediction market where users trade on sports, political and economic event outcomes, majority-owned by its founder.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 9bn (Feb 2026); ICE agreed to invest up to USD 2bn in Oct 2025
sponsorships: NHL official prediction market partner (multiyear, Oct 2025)
markets: Global users outside banned countries; returned to US customers after CFTC settlement in Dec 2025; sports are 63% of trades

signals.regions: Reopened to US customers after CFTC settlement (Dec 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymarket)

rationale: Sports-led platform with NHL deal and global user base; blocked in France, Brazil, Italy and other countries, which limits F1 race-market activation.

name: Underdog
desc: US fantasy sports pick'em operator that has also launched online sportsbooks in several states.
capacity_detail: Valued at USD 1.23bn in USD 100m Series C led by Spark Capital, Mar 2025
markets: Fantasy products in 41 US states; sportsbooks in North Carolina, Missouri, New Jersey and Delaware
rationale: Unicorn chasing US sports bettors against FanDuel and DraftKings; F1's young US fans fit, but brand spend so far is domestic.

name: Fanatics Betting & Gaming
desc: Sports betting and iGaming arm of privately held Fanatics, also running Fanatics Markets prediction contracts.
ownership: private, owner not stated (unit of privately held Fanatics)
capacity_detail: Betting and gaming account for roughly USD 2bn of annual revenue (Jan 2026)
markets: US state-licensed sportsbook and casino, including Missouri from Dec 2025; prediction contracts in 24 US states
rationale: Fanatics links merchandise and betting; F1 licensing and US races could cross-sell its sportsbook to motorsport fans.

name: 1xBet
desc: Curacao-licensed online betting operator with undisclosed owners, active mainly in Africa, Latin America and Asia.
capacity_detail: FC Barcelona sponsor until 2029; ATP Challenger Tour official betting partner from Oct 2025
sponsorships: FC Barcelona (to 2029); ATP Challenger Tour (from Oct 2025); Billie Jean King Cup (to 2026); Barcelona SC Ecuador (2025); PSG (2022-2025)
markets: Claims licences in 35+ markets in Latin America, Africa and Western Europe; banned in US, UK, Russia, France, Spain
rationale: Buys global football and tennis rights, but owner opacity, UK licence revocation and bans make F1 association very unlikely.
